Frederick D. Haynes III

Democratic candidate for U.S. Representative, District 30, Dallas County, Texas · Open seat

Senior Pastor, Friendship-West Baptist Church (Dallas)

Frederick D. Haynes III is the senior pastor of Friendship-West Baptist Church in southern Dallas, a role he has held for more than 40 years, and a first-time candidate for public office. He won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary for the open Texas 30th Congressional District seat with about 73% of the vote, defeating Barbara Mallory Caraway and Rodney LaBruce. He faces Republican Everett Jackson in the November 3, 2026 general election for the seat Jasmine Crockett left to run for the U.S. Senate.

Where III stands

Economy and jobs
Names lowering the cost of living as his top priority. Says he would reduce energy, housing and health care costs through targeted tax relief, supply chain solutions and policies that do not burden working families.
Housing
Calls affordability the district's biggest issue. Supports policies to expand housing supply and affordability and to protect working families and seniors.
Federal spending
Says federal programs should be efficient and responsive to local needs.
Health care
Named health care for all as a priority at his campaign kickoff.
Immigration enforcement
Named abolishing U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) as a priority at his campaign kickoff.

Background

  • Senior Pastor, Friendship-West Baptist Church, Dallas (more than 40 years)
  • President and CEO, Rainbow PUSH Coalition (2024; resigned in April 2024 after less than three months)
  • No previous elected office sought or held before 2026
  • Has lived in Texas for 43 years
  • Won the 2026 Democratic primary for TX-30 (about 72.6%)
